subject: Franska 3
title: Relative pronouns: qui, que, où and dont
sourceSummary: Building more advanced, complex sentences with the relative pronouns qui, que, où and dont.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct pronoun: "C'est le professeur ___ nous a donné ce livre."
questions.opener: Is the pronoun a subject or an object in the clause? Test it: who gave the book?
questions.explanation: "Qui" is the subject of the clause (it's the teacher WHO gave the book) — the verb "a donné" follows it directly.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct pronoun: "Le livre ___ tu m'as prêté est vraiment intéressant."
questions.opener: Here the pronoun is an object — who is doing the action? "Tu" is, and the book is what's received.
questions.explanation: "Que" is the object of the clause ("tu m'as prêté LE LIVRE") — it's followed by subject + verb ("tu m'as prêté"), unlike "qui", which is followed directly by a verb.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct pronoun: "C'est la ville ___ j'ai passé mon enfance."
questions.explanation: "Où" is used for place (and time): "la ville où j'ai passé mon enfance" means "the city where I spent my childhood".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct pronoun: "Voici le livre ___ je t'ai parlé." (I talked ABOUT the book — parler DE quelque chose)
questions.opener: Which preposition belongs to the verb "parler de"?
questions.explanation: "Dont" replaces "de + something": "parler de quelque chose" → "le livre dont je t'ai parlé" (the book I've talked about).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct pronoun: "Les élèves ___ ont réussi l'examen étaient très contents."
questions.opener: The subject of the clause again — who passed the exam?
questions.explanation: "Qui" is the subject: it's the students WHO passed the exam. Note that "qui" is never shortened to "qu'" before a vowel, unlike "que".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct pronoun: "C'est la femme ___ la fille est médecin." (the woman WHOSE daughter is a doctor)
questions.opener: "Dont" can also express ownership/belonging, like English "whose".
questions.explanation: "Dont" can correspond to English "whose": "la femme dont la fille est médecin" means "the woman whose daughter is a doctor". Word order after "dont" doesn't change: dont + subject + verb.

questions.prompt: Combine the two sentences into one, using the correct relative pronoun: "J'ai un ami. Cet ami habite à Lyon et je lui rends visite chaque été."
questions.opener: Think about what role "cet ami" plays in the second clause — subject, or something else?
questions.answer: J'ai un ami qui habite à Lyon et à qui je rends visite chaque été.
steps: First part: "cet ami habite à Lyon" — here "ami" is the subject of the clause → "qui habite à Lyon".
Second part: "je lui rends visite" — "lui" is an indirect object (rendre visite À quelqu'un), not a plain "que" object.
An indirect object with à + a person requires "à qui", not "que": "à qui je rends visite".
Full sentence: "J'ai un ami qui habite à Lyon et à qui je rends visite chaque été." Note that you may need two different relative constructions in the same sentence depending on each word's role.

questions.prompt: How do you choose between qui, que, où and dont?
questions.opener: Four pronouns, four roles in the clause.
questions.answer: qui = subject of the clause, followed directly by a verb (l'homme qui parle). que = object of the clause, followed by subject + verb (l'homme que je vois) — shortens to qu' before a vowel. où = place or time (la ville où j'habite, le jour où c'est arrivé). dont = replaces de + something: a verb with the preposition de (parler de, avoir besoin de, être content de) or ownership/belonging (whose) — dont is always followed by subject + verb, with no inversion. Memory rule: qui does something, que receives something, où is a place, dont goes with de.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct pronoun: "La chanson ___ j'écoute en ce moment est géniale."
questions.opener: Who is doing the action "listen"? "Je" is, and the song is what's received.
questions.explanation: "Que" is the object (I'm listening to the song) and is followed by subject + verb: "que j'écoute".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct pronoun: "Les amis ___ viennent dîner ce soir sont très sympas."
questions.explanation: "Qui" is the subject (the friends WHO are coming) and is followed directly by the verb "viennent".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct pronoun: "Le jour ___ nous nous sommes rencontrés était pluvieux."
questions.opener: Is this about a point in time?
questions.explanation: "Où" is also used for time: "le jour où" means "the day when".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct pronoun: "C'est un sujet ___ on parle beaucoup en ce moment."
questions.opener: Which preposition belongs to the verb "parler de"?
questions.explanation: "Dont" replaces "de + something": "parler de quelque chose" → "un sujet dont on parle".

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly combines: "J'ai un chat. J'adore ce chat."?
questions.opener: Who is doing the action "love"? "J'" is, and the cat is what's received.
questions.explanation: "Que" is the object (I love the cat) and is followed by subject + verb: "que j'adore".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct pronoun: "C'est l'outil ___ j'ai besoin pour ce travail."
questions.opener: Which preposition belongs to the expression "avoir besoin de"?
questions.explanation: "Avoir besoin de quelque chose" is replaced with "dont": "l'outil dont j'ai besoin" (the tool I need).

questions.prompt: How do you decide whether to use "qui" or "que"?
questions.opener: Think about the pronoun's role in the clause, not whether it refers to a person or a thing.
choices: "Qui" is followed directly by a verb (subject), "que" is followed by subject + verb (object)
"Qui" is always for things, "que" always for people
"Qui" is only used in the plural
questions.explanation: Both "qui" and "que" can refer to people or things — the difference is the pronoun's role: "qui" is the subject (followed directly by a verb), "que" is the object (followed by subject + verb).
